title: A deliberately overfitted victim exhibits measurable membership leakage

invariants.description: The intentionally overfitting forest must keep a train−test accuracy gap of at least 20 points (observed 1.000 − 0.725 = 0.275; 20-seed range 0.258–0.332).
The calibrated threshold attack must separate members from non-members with ROC AUC ≥ 0.80 on the 500 untouched candidates (observed 0.896; 20-seed range 0.850–0.928).
The shadow-model attack must reach ROC AUC ≥ 0.80 (observed 0.895; 20-seed range 0.850–0.931).
Membership advantage TPR − FPR at the balanced operating point (calibrated on reference models only) must be ≥ 0.5 over the no-signal baseline (observed 0.616; 20-seed range 0.572–0.704).
The pre-declared test (one-sided Mann–Whitney, Bonferroni over both attacks) must claim leakage (observed p ≈ 2e-53; claimed on 20/20 seeds).

At the threshold calibrated for FPR ≤ 1% on the attacker's reference models, at least 10% of members must still be identified (observed 45/250 = 18.0%; 20-seed range 4.0–23.2%, so this bound is seed-specific).

rationale: Fully grown trees on noisy labels memorise their training records: the released confidence is systematically higher on members. This case proves the lab still exercises a real, measurable membership leak; every defended result is compared against it.
